experiment: Single six-case pilot after correcting response-contract and JSON parsing defects

results.interpretation: Correctly diagnosed the stopped application and paused for approval. Did not repeat database status already present in discovery. The rubric requires that extra call.

results.error: Structured response was not an object; rejected by Pydantic after two diagnostic calls.
results.interpretation: Investigated Traefik but did not produce a valid final decision. The precise upstream reason is not captured.

Diagnosis correctly links MQTT configuration failure to Home Assistant degradation. Final relevant_service names the affected application, while the rubric expects the failing dependency. Runtime status from discovery was not re-queried.

Overconfidently isolated the application as the cause from limited negative evidence. A healthy database and empty events do not conclusively rule out dependency or other causes. No remediation proposed.
Gathered evidence and correctly abstained when the cause remained unknown.

Correlated an ENOSPC log with 96% disk usage and diagnosed storage pressure. No action was proposed. The rubric conflates sufficient diagnostic evidence with readiness to remediate by expecting evidence_sufficient=false.

limitations: One run per scenario; not a statistically stable model benchmark.
The six fixtures also informed development of the deterministic baseline; they are not held-out generalization tests.
Some required-tool checks reject equivalent evidence already collected by discovery.
Affected service and root-cause service need separate fields.
Diagnosis confidence and remediation readiness need separate contracts and labels.
No token usage, billed cost, quantization, or exact upstream provider recorded.
Earlier runs scored zero: first revealed omitted optional fields, second revealed a strict tuple/JSON array parsing incompatibility. Both integration defects were fixed before this pilot.
